title: Google named the new boss of Gemini 4. Both of Gemini’s co-leads quit the same day
excerpt: Demis Hassabis is handing over Google DeepMind. Jeff Dean, Oriol Vinyals, Quoc Le and Sanjay Ghemawat are leaving to found Discovery Loop.
content_html:
Sundar Pichai’s memo on Wednesday thanked Jeff Dean for “an incredible 27-year run” and said he was off to start a company with Sanjay Ghemawat. He posted the same two names on X. Discovery Loop’s website names four. The two Google skipped are Quoc Le, who co-founded Google Brain, and Oriol Vinyals, whose X bio reads “Gemini co-lead”.

Dean’s own LinkedIn says “Gemini overall co-technical lead”.

So on the day Google named the executive who will build Gemini 4, both of Gemini’s co-technical leads walked out.

The part Google did announce

Demis Hassabis is giving up the day-to-day running of Google DeepMind. He becomes its chair and chief scientist of Alphabet, keeps Isomorphic Labs, and moves into DeepMind’s new Platform 37 offices in London. Koray Kavukcuoglu, the lab’s technology chief, takes over as senior vice president and reports straight to Pichai. He gets Gemini 4, CNBC reported.

Kavukcuoglu has spent 13 years at DeepMind. He started its deep learning team and led the work behind WaveNet and DQN. He is not an outsider parachuted in, and nobody has questioned the choice.

The departures were paragraph four.

Thirteen years, one email

Vinyals said goodbye on X, and the note is worth reading twice. He arrived at Google 13 years ago after “a quick email exchange” with Dean. He worked on seq2seq and distillation, then co-led AlphaStar and Gemini.

Then the twist. “The best part? The same person who brought me in is challenging me to take the next leap.”

Dean recruited him in 2013 and has now recruited him out.

A company with no office

Discovery Loop barely exists yet. Steven Levy, who interviewed all four for Wired, reports the idea came together only weeks ago. There are no staff and nowhere to sit. “Our immediate order of business is to find office space,” Dean wrote.

The timing is almost too neat. On 25 July, Dean stood in front of 6,000 would-be founders at Y Combinator’s Startup School and gave a talk billed as the number one rule for building in AI. The interviewer asked what areas startups should tackle. Eleven days later he announced his own.

They pitched a handful of VC firms with a deck. Few founders have a prior-work slide that lists TensorFlow and TPUs.

The bet: AI as the researcher

“Scientific discovery is bottlenecked,” the site argues. Not the method, which it calls one of humanity’s great inventions, but the execution. Someone still has to propose an experiment, run it, read the results, and go again, one loop at a time.

Discovery Loop wants to automate the loop and run thousands in parallel. It starts with machine learning research, then does something telling: it points those capabilities at its own stack and becomes its own first customer. Only then does it go after the National Academy of Engineering’s Grand Challenges, from better medicines to clean water to securing cyberspace.

Le, who spent years automating model design at Google, sees the first target clearly. “It might be that we will discover a different transformer architecture,” he told Wired.

Vinyals named the hole in the plan. “One of the things that we’ll be obviously very focused on is how these models come up with new ideas to try,” he said. “That’s not something that currently they’re super strong at.”

Vinod Khosla, who is funding it, was less measured. Backing the four could produce something “larger than the impact that Google had”, he wrote. His thesis, as he put it to Wired, is a swap of roles. People have been using AI to do research. Here, AI is the researcher.

Alphabet is on the cap table

This is not a raid, and Google is not pretending otherwise. Radical Ventures and Khosla Ventures co-led the seed round. Lightspeed, Kleiner Perkins, Doerr Capital and Alphabet itself joined, and the New York Times reports Google holds a stake. Nobody is disclosing the size or the valuation.

Radical’s Jordan Jacobs takes a board seat. Google is the cloud partner and will supply the compute for year one. It also wants a joint research framework on machine learning systems.

“Jeff and Sanjay helped to drive some of the most significant technology transitions,” Pichai wrote, “from our early search infrastructure to the neural networks that helped create the modern AI era.” Warm, and entirely true. It still names two.

The market read it as subtraction

Alphabet fell around 5%, touching $362.31 in New York, Bloomberg reported. It called the overhaul seismic and said it cast doubt over the leadership of a critical growth area just as competition sharpens.

The backdrop is unhelpful. Google’s next flagship model has slipped several times this year, Business Insider reported, including one Gemini Pro delay over coding performance. The company also turned cash flow negative for the first time on record last quarter, while guiding to capital spending of up to $205bn.

The commentary ran harsher than the coverage. “Game over,” wrote Tae Kim, calling Dean and Hassabis the two most important AI executives at Google. The researcher Nathan Lambert reckoned the episode will be studied for years as the incumbent that held every advantage and could not get moving. Axios was cooler and no kinder, placing the reshuffle inside a company “struggling to keep pace with OpenAI and Anthropic”.

Not everyone read a verdict. Steven Sinofsky, who once ran Windows, called the four’s work truly generational. He noted that fusing research with product has been a brass ring of corporate labs for as long as computer science has existed. Researchers leaving to build is the oldest story in the industry.

Google’s own numbers cut the other way too. The Gemini app is past 950 million monthly users and Gemma downloads are past 900 million, a quarter after Pichai told doubters Google is not losing the AI race.

Hassabis goes long

Hassabis framed his move as a choice about where to spend himself. “We have arrived at a pivotal moment in human history,” he wrote. “I’ve been working towards AGI my whole life and now, like many of you, I feel it is close at hand.” He wanted the time and space for the big picture rather than daily operations.

The rest goes to drug discovery. “It’s time for AI to prove its unequivocal value to the world, and what better way to demonstrate that than to help finally cure diseases like cancer.” Isomorphic, now moving into trials, is where that claim gets settled.

One detail travels badly from California. Alphabet’s chief scientist, the person it has put in charge of thinking about AGI, will be sitting in London.

Two companies, one claim

Put Wednesday’s two documents side by side and the same boast appears in both.

Pichai’s memo calls Google “the only company that has the full stack”, world-class at every layer from infrastructure to frontier models to applications. Discovery Loop’s site says its founders have “true full-stack depth that spans chips, hardware infrastructure, software infrastructure, ML models, and products”.

One of those companies employs tens of thousands of people. The other has four and no office. Their shared credit list runs from Search and MapReduce through Spanner, TensorFlow, TPUs, AlphaFold and Gemini, which makes the claim cheeky rather than absurd.

None of this is new pressure on Google. TNW has covered the morale and talent strain inside DeepMind before. What is new is the arithmetic: one promotion announced, four researchers gone.

The site closes on the line Google will find hardest to answer. “Imagine a future where a handful of people can conduct scientific research and engineering tasks much more rapidly, and with higher quality, than massive teams of scientists and engineers do today.”

Four people just left a massive team to test it, on compute Google is selling them, with Alphabet’s money in the round. Gemini 4 will tell us who was right.

content_html_zh:
桑达尔·皮查伊 (Sundar Pichai) 周三在备忘录中感谢杰夫·迪恩 (Jeff Dean) “令人难以置信的 27 年业绩”，并表示他将与桑杰·格马瓦特 (Sanjay Ghemawat) 一起创办一家公司。 他在 X 上发布了相同的两个名字。 Discovery Loop 的网站列出了四个。 谷歌跳过的两位是谷歌大脑联合创始人 Quoc Le 和 Oriol Vinyals，他的 X 简历上写着“双子座联合领导”。

Dean 自己的 LinkedIn 上写着“Gemini 整体联合技术领先”。

因此，在 Google 任命负责构建 Gemini 4 的高管的那天，Gemini 的两位联合技术主管都辞职了。

谷歌确实宣布的部分

Demis Hassabis 将放弃 Google DeepMind 的日常运营。 他成为 Alphabet 的主席兼首席科学家，保留同构实验室，并搬进 DeepMind 在伦敦的新 Platform 37 办公室。 该实验室技术主管 Koray Kavukcuoglu 接任高级副总裁，直接向皮查伊汇报。 据 CNBC 报道，他得到了 Gemini 4。

Kavukcuoglu 在 DeepMind 工作了 13 年。 他创办了深度学习团队并领导了 WaveNet 和 DQN 背后的工作。 他不是空降而来的局外人，也没有人质疑他的选择。

偏离的是第四段。

十三年，一封电子邮件

Vinyals 在 X 上告别了，这篇笔记值得读两遍。 13 年前，在与 Dean 进行“快速电子邮件交流”后，他加入了 Google。 他致力于 seq2seq 和蒸馏，然后共同领导 AlphaStar 和 Gemini。

然后是扭曲。 “最好的部分？ 引进我的那个人正在挑战我迈出下一步。”

Dean在2013年招募了他，现在已经把他挖走了。

没有办公室的公司

探索环路还几乎不存在。 史蒂文·利维（Steven Levy）接受了《连线》杂志的采访，他表示这个想法是在几周前产生的。 没有工作人员，也没有地方可以坐。 “我们的当务之急是寻找办公空间，”迪恩写道。

时机几乎太整齐了。 7 月 25 日，Dean 站在 Y Combinator 创业学校的 6,000 名潜在创始人面前，发表了一场被誉为人工智能建设第一条规则的演讲。 面试官问初创公司应该解决哪些领域。 十一天后，他宣布了自己的决定。

他们向几家风险投资公司推销了一套方案。 很少有创始人拥有列出 TensorFlow 和 TPU 的先前工作幻灯片。

赌注：人工智能作为研究人员

该网站认为，“科学发现遇到了瓶颈”。 不是它所说的人类伟大发明之一的方法，而是执行。 仍然需要有人提出一项实验，运行它，读取结果，然后再次进行，一次一个循环。

Discovery Loop 希望自动化循环并并行运行数千个。 它从机器学习研究开始，然后做了一些有意义的事情：它将这些功能指向自己的堆栈，并成为自己的第一个客户。 只有这样，它才能应对美国国家工程院的重大挑战，从更好的药物到清洁的水，再到确保网络空间的安全。

Le 在 Google 工作了数年自动化模型设计，他清楚地看到了第一个目标。 “我们可能会发现一种不同的变压器架构，”他告诉《连线》杂志。

维尼亚尔斯在计划中命名了这个洞。 “我们显然会非常关注的一件事是这些模型如何提出新的想法来尝试，”他说。 “这不是他们目前超级擅长的事情。”

资助该项目的维诺德·科斯拉(Vinod Khosla)则没有那么谨慎。 他写道，支持这四家可能会产生“比谷歌更大的影响”。 正如他向《连线》杂志所说的那样，他的论文是角色的互换。 人们一直在使用人工智能进行研究。 在这里，人工智能是研究者。

字母表在上限表上

这不是一次突袭，谷歌也没有假装不是。 Radical Ventures 和 Khosla Ventures 共同领投了种子轮融资。 Lightspeed、Kleiner Perkins、Doerr Capital 和 Alphabet 本身也加入其中，据《纽约时报》报道，谷歌持有股份。 没有人透露其规模或估值。

Radical 的乔丹·雅各布斯 (Jordan Jacobs) 获得董事会席位。 谷歌是云合作伙伴，将提供第一年的计算服务。 它还希望建立一个关于机器学习系统的联合研究框架。

“杰夫和桑杰帮助推动了一些最重要的技术转型，”皮查伊写道，“从我们早期的搜索基础设施到帮助创建现代人工智能时代的神经网络。” 温暖，而且完全真实。 它仍然命名两个。

市场将其解读为减法

据彭博社报道，Alphabet 在纽约股市下跌约 5%，触及 362.31 美元。 该公司称此次改革是令人震惊的，并表示，在竞争加剧之际，这让人们对关键增长领域的领导地位产生了怀疑。

背景没有帮助。 据 Business Insider 报道，谷歌的下一代旗舰机型今年已经多次下滑，其中包括一款 Gemini Pro 在编码性能上的延迟。 上季度，该公司还首次将现金流转为负数，同时引导资本支出高达 2050 亿美元。

评论比报道更严厉。 “游戏结束了”，Tae Kim 写道，并称 Dean 和 Hassabis 是谷歌最重要的两位人工智能高管。 研究人员内森·兰伯特（Nathan Lambert）认为，这一事件将被研究多年，因为现任总统占据了一切优势，无法行动。 Axios 更酷，也更友善，将重组置于一家“努力跟上 OpenAI 和 Anthropic 步伐”的公司内部。

并不是每个人都宣读了判决。 曾经运行 Windows 的史蒂文·辛诺夫斯基 (Steven Sinofsky) 称这四人的工作真正具有时代意义。 他指出，自从计算机科学存在以来，将研究与产品融合一直是企业实验室的一个重要组成部分。 研究人员离开去建造是该行业最古老的故事。

谷歌自己的数据也有相反的情况。 Gemini 应用程序的月用户量已超过 9.5 亿，Gemma 的下载量也已超过 9 亿，而四分之一前，皮查伊告诉质疑者谷歌不会输掉人工智能竞赛。

哈萨比斯走得很远

哈萨比斯将他的举动视为自己选择去哪里度过。 “我们已经到达了人类历史上的关键时刻，”他写道。 “我一生都在为通用人工智能而努力，现在，像你们中的许多人一样，我觉得它已经近在咫尺。” 他想要的是大局的时间和空间，而不是日常运营。

其余的用于药物发现。 “现在是人工智能向世界证明其明确价值的时候了，还有什么比帮助最终治愈癌症等疾病更好的方式来证明这一点呢？” 现在进入试验阶段的 Isomorphic 就是这一说法得到解决的地方。

加利福尼亚州传出的一个细节很糟糕。 Alphabet 的首席科学家、负责 AGI 思考的人将坐在伦敦。

两家公司，一家索赔

把周三的两份文件放在一起看，两份文件都出现了同样的夸耀。

皮查伊的备忘录称谷歌是“唯一一家拥有完整堆栈的公司”，从基础设施到前沿模型再到应用程序的各个层面都是世界一流的。 Discovery Loop 的网站称其创始人拥有“真正的全栈深度，涵盖芯片、硬件基础设施、软件基础设施、机器学习模型和产品”。

其中一家公司拥有数万名员工。 另一个有四个人，没有办公室。 他们共享的功绩清单涵盖从 Search 和 MapReduce 到 Spanner、TensorFlow、TPU、AlphaFold 和 Gemini，这使得这一说法显得厚颜无耻，而不是荒谬。

这些都不是谷歌面临的新压力。 TNW 之前曾报道过 DeepMind 内部的士气和人才压力。 新鲜的是算术：宣布一名晋升，四名研究人员离职。

该网站即将关闭，谷歌将发现最难回答的问题。 “想象一下未来，少数人可以比今天的大量科学家和工程师团队更快、更高质量地开展科学研究和工程任务。”

四个人刚刚离开一个庞大的团队来测试它，谷歌正在出售他们的计算能力，Alphabet 的资金也在其中。 双子座 4 号会告诉我们谁是对的。
